title: Don't Boycott GTA 6, Say Fired Rockstar Workers, Suggest Buying T-Shirts Instead
description: Workers fired by Rockstar Games in an alleged union-busting move have urged players not to boycott GTA 6, but to buy T-shirts to fund their legal battle.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 6 Labor Dispute: Fired Workers Urge Fans Not to Boycott

As anticipation for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 continues to build worldwide, internal labor issues at Rockstar Games have once again brought the company into the spotlight. According to a report by gaming media outlet Eurogamer, the workers who were fired by Rockstar Games in an alleged 'union-busting' move last autumn have come forward with a clear message for the gaming community: please do not boycott the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

### A Call Against a Boycott

In the gaming industry, consumer boycotts are a common reaction when developers or publishers face controversies, layoffs, or labor disputes. However, the former Rockstar employees directly affected by these actions have chosen a different approach. Despite their termination, which they attribute to union-busting efforts last autumn, they are asking concerned players not to withhold their support from the highly anticipated sequel.

This perspective offers a unique dynamic for GTA 6, a title that dominates industry conversations. The workers' stance suggests a separation between their ongoing disputes with corporate management and the massive creative and collaborative effort behind the game itself.

### Supporting the Legal Battle Through Merchandise

While they are asking fans not to boycott GTA 6, the fired workers are still in need of assistance as they fight their termination. Instead of disrupting the game's launch, they have suggested an alternative way for supporters to help: purchasing a T-shirt. 

By buying these items, concerned individuals can directly help fund the ongoing legal battle that these workers are facing. It provides a direct, practical avenue for fans who want to stand in solidarity with the workers without resorting to sweeping consumer boycotts that affect the broader gaming ecosystem.

## Editor's Take

It is refreshing to see such pragmatism from workers facing a difficult situation with a major gaming publisher. By asking fans not to boycott GTA 6 while offering a constructive way to support their legal fight through merchandise, they are charting a mature path forward. For players, supporting the workers through these targeted fundraising efforts while enjoying the game allows for a balanced approach to supporting both labor rights and the medium.
